source: create a game where users cam fly all kinds of vehicles & they will get points after hitting the CP written boards on various similar looking buildings.

answers.ask: No theme was stated - modern city, military airfield, or something stylized?
answers.answer: Use a small modern city with similar-looking buildings and rooftop/side checkpoint boards.

answers.ask: Is this a timed score attack, a race between players to the highest score, or endless free flight?
answers.answer: Make it endless free flight: players earn points whenever they hit checkpoint boards, with their score tracked on a leaderboard.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] theme — Q: No theme was stated - modern city, military airfield, or something stylized? A: Use a small modern city with similar-looking buildings and rooftop/side checkpoint boards.
- [author] goal — Q: Is this a timed score attack, a race between players to the highest score, or endless free flight? A: Make it endless free flight: players earn points whenever they hit checkpoint boards, with their score tracked on a leaderboard.
- [agent_inferred] vehicle launch — Q: Where should vehicles enter the flying space? A: Use one clear rooftop launch pad at the edge of the city, sized for the largest supported vehicle and facing open air.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a small modern 3D city built as an open free-flight volume among clusters of similar-looking buildings. Mount multiple clearly readable boards labeled “CP” on rooftops and building sides, varying their heights and approach directions so flying vehicles can hit them without following a fixed route. Keep broad open-air corridors between buildings and place one large rooftop launch pad at the city edge facing into clear air. The experience is endless, so include no finish line or terminal destination; compose the towers, side boards, rooftop boards, and launch pad so their vertical relationships are legible.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Simulation, specifically free aircraft and vehicle operation. It is not Racing because there is no route, lap, or finish.

## Shape and preset
Use `volume-open-air`, named Open Airspace: the playable space is the 3D volume between and above buildings, with rooftops serving as discrete landing surfaces. Preset is none; Aircraft Operation would add jobs, a progression hub, and gates not requested by this endless free-flight concept.

## Config requirements
Use universal `settlement-density` for the compact modern building cluster. Use the visible side of `trigger-scoring`, taken from Sports and routed as a visible goal board plus an invisible detection plane, for every rooftop and facade board labeled “CP.” Use the visible side of `spawn-area` for the edge-of-city rooftop launch pad. Buildings intentionally share a similar architectural language rather than relying on a unique landmark.

## Layout requirements
Place one `spawn-area` vehicle launch marker on the rooftop pad, oriented toward unobstructed air and sized for the largest vehicle. For every visible `trigger-scoring` board, align a detection plane directly to its face and leave a collision-free approach and exit volume. Distribute boards across multiple heights and building sides without imposing an ordered route. No finish, lap, checkpoint-respawn, or winner zone is needed.

## Layout components
One compact city contains repeated modern buildings, open aerial corridors, multiple rooftop and side-mounted CP boards, and one large perimeter rooftop launch pad. Boards face varied but reachable approach directions. The building cluster defines the horizontal boundary, while the flight ceiling and outer air envelope define the volumetric limits.

## Render order
Use `isometric`: vertical board placement, rooftop landings, facade approaches, and open-air corridors must be readable together.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
The scale band is medium because a small building cluster must coexist with individually readable checkpoint boards. The theme is a clean modern city of similar-looking buildings. Use `CHECK` for volumetric flight among structures; no separate maps or interior transitions are required.
